chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether from Ali bin Mahziyar, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that the reports have differed from your forefathers (peace be upon him) regarding the complete [prayer] and the shortening in the two Harams. So, from these is that one should complete the prayer, even if it is just one [rak'ah], and from these is that one should shorten for as long as one does not intend to stay for ten days. And I did not cease to be upon the complete [prayer] therein until we commenced with our Hajj in this year of ours. So, the jurists of our companions advised me with the shortening when I did not intend staying for ten days. So I came to be shortening, and have been distressed by that, until I recognize your view.

So he wrote to me in his own handwriting: 'I have taught you, may Allah have Mercy on you, the merits of the prayer in the two Harams over the other places, therefore I love for you that when you enter these two, that you should not shorten, and frequently pray the prayer in these two Harams'.

So I said to him orally, after two years, 'I wrote to you with such and such, and you answered me with such and such'. So he said: 'Yes'. I said, 'Which thing did you mean by the two Harams?' So he said: 'Makkah and Al-Medina'.

key_terms.التَّقْصِير: Shortening the prayer (praying two rak'ahs instead of four)
key_terms.الْإِتْمَام: Completing the prayer (praying four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Harams (sanctuaries), specifically identified here as Mecca and Medina
key_terms.مُقَامَ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: Intending to stay for ten days (a condition for shortening prayers in fiqh)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on shortening prayers in Mecca and Medina according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This correspondence highlights the scholarly debate between the default rule of shortening prayers (qasr) for travelers and the specific recommendation to offer complete prayers (tamam) in the two holy sanctuaries, reflecting the Imam’s preference for maximizing reward in these sacred spaces. Notably, the Imam explicitly defines the 'two Harams' in this context as Mecca and Medina, a clarification that aids jurists in applying the ruling to the primary sites of pilgrimage and residence. The narrative underscores the practical application of hadith by a companion who shifted his practice based on scholarly advice before receiving the Imam’s direct preference.

en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from all from Ali ibn Mahziyar from who has said the following:

“I once wrote to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that Ahadith from your ancestors about performing Salat (prayer) in the two al-Haram (the Sacred places) in complete form exist in disagreement. Certain ones say that it is in complete form even if it is just one Salat (prayer) and others say that it is in reduced form unless you decide to stay there for ten days. I however continue to perform in complete form until this year during our al-Hajj, when our scholars of fiqh advised me to perform in reduced form because I did not intend to stay for ten days; so I turned to reduced form and I remain stressed until I receive your instruction.

He (the Imam) wrote to me with his own hand writing, ‘You have come to know, may Allah grant you blessings, of the virtue of the performing Salat (prayer) in the two al-Haram (the Sacred places), over the other places; thus I like for you that when you enter them not to perform your Salat (prayer) in reduced form. You should perform a great deal of Salat (prayer) therein.’

I then after two years spoke to him about it face to face saying, ‘I wrote to you about such and such issues and you answered as such and such.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, so it was.’ I then asked, ‘What do you mean by the two al-Haram (the Sacred places)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is Makkah and al-Madinah.’” NOTE: Fatwa best explains Hadith 2-8 of this Chapter)
